title: About Me
About Me
text:
Environmentalism
I first became passionate about environmentalism after a speaker came to my 8th grade classroom to discuss the impact of the meat industry on global warming. Since then I have been a vegetarian and have been an advocate for animal rights.
I am very interested in intertidal ecology and how climate change will impact these ecosystems and am hopeful to work with a research lab in the near future on this topic. I am also generally interested in how to transfer to carbon neutral living at the community level. If anyone is interested in talking about environmentalism and climate change feel free to email me!

title: Greenhouse Experiment
text:
Stipa pulchra Greenhouse Experiment
Spring quarter 2026 I interned with the Cheadle Center for Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration to help plan and begin a greenhouse experiment. The purpose of this experiment was to test Stipa pulchra survivorship in response to varying salinity levels. This experiment was done to investigate a hypothesis looking at why Stipa pulchra had seen die off at the North Campus Open Space restoration site in recent years. The experimental design included four salinity treatments with wet versus dry treatments for 80 individual plants.
My work in this project mainly involved the experimental design, data collection, salinity treatment, and creating preliminary visualizations for the data collected. My work on the project ended after spring quarter 2026, but the project continued after this. The figure below is a preliminary data visualization I created for the project. The figure caption was written by me for this website, and the visualization was done in R. Additional preliminary visualizations along with the original Quarto Documents are in the Elises_work folder on the project’s GitHub repository.


View code
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
library(here)
# reading in files
leaf_count <- read.csv(here("data", "Stipa_salinity_experiment_data - survival_leaves_2026_05_27.csv")) |>
  
# cleaning data 

  # cleaning names 
  clean_names() |> 
  # selecting for desired columns
  select(
    water, 
    live_leaves,
    green_leaves, 
    salinity) |> 
  # remove rows with missing values (NAs) to keep the graph clean
  drop_na(live_leaves, green_leaves) |> 
  # calculating proportion of live leaves using mutate
  mutate(
    proportion_live = live_leaves / (live_leaves + green_leaves),
    salinity = as.factor(salinity)
  )

# creating preliminary visualization

# base layer 
ggplot(leaf_count,
       # looking at salinity on the x axis, proprtion_live on y axis
       # filling by treatment
       mapping = aes(x = salinity,
                     y = proportion_live,
                     fill = water)) +
  # first layer: geom_boxplot
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5,
               position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  # second layer: geom_jitter
  geom_jitter(
    # coloring by treatment
    aes(color = water),
    # adjusting positioning and size
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.8),
    alpha = 0.7,
    size = 2,
    shape = 21
  ) +
  # adding title, subtitle, naming axes 
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Live Leaves by Salinity and Water Treatment",
    subtitle = "Data from 5/27/2026 and 5/28/2026",
    x = "Salinity Treatment (dS/m)",
    y = "Proportion of Live Leaves",
    fill = "Watering Treatment"
  ) +
  # adding theme
  theme_minimal() +
  # removing legend for readability
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  # adding custom colors for boxplot and jitter
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("wet" = "skyblue3", "dry" = "darkkhaki")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("wet" = "skyblue3", "dry" = "darkkhaki")
  )









Proportion of Live Leaves by Salinity and Water Treatment: Wet treatments are indicated in blue; dry treatments in yellow. Individual observations are represented by points, with box plots displaying the median and interquartile range (IQR) for each treatment group. Data collected by Elise LaFreniere and Abriel Lau; visualization generated by Elise LaFreniere.

title: Film Photography
text:
I first started film photography when I was 15 years old on a point and shoot my parents got me for Christmas. I love capturing the world, my friends, and even myself through the lens of a camera. Featured in this map are photos taken on my Canon AE-1 on 35mm Kodak gold film.
Displayed is an interactive map showing locations where I have taken my photos. The map centers around Isla Vista but includes photos from Santa Barbara, Catalina Island, the bay, and New York.


Code
# loading in packages
library(leaflet)
library(tidyverse)

# creating object gps to store photo data 
gps <- read_csv("data/photo_gps_updated.csv")

# creating gps grouped data
gps_grouped <- gps |> 
  group_by(location, latitude, longitude) |> 
  summarize(
    # creating thumbnails 
    popup_content = paste0(
      '<div style="max-width: 280px; text-align: center;">',
        '<h4 style="margin: 0 0 10px 0; font-family: inherit; font-size: 14px;">', unique(location), '</h4>',
        '<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; justify-content: center;">',
          paste0(
          '<div style="text-align: center; width: 100%;">',
              '<a href="images/', filename, '" class="lightbox" data-gallery="map-gallery" title="', desc, '">',
                '<img src="images/', filename, '" style="width: 120px; height: 120px; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);"/>',
              '</a>',
              '<p style="margin: 4px 0 0 0; font-size: 12px; color: #555; font-style: italic; max-width: 200px; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;">', desc, '</p>',
            '</div>',
            collapse = ""
          ),
        '</div>',
      '</div>'
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# generate the interactive map layout
site_map <- leaflet(data = gps_grouped) |>  
  
  # Add base map layers
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "ESRI World Imagery") |>  
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.OceanBasemap, group = "ESRI Oceans") |> 
  
  # add mini map
  addMiniMap(toggleDisplay = TRUE, minimized = TRUE) |> 
  
  # Center map at Isla Vista area
  setView(lng = -119.83, lat = 34.44, zoom = 10) |> 
  
# add location bubbles and markers 
  addMarkers(clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(),
             lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude,
             popup = ~popup_content) |> 

  # add layers control 
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("ESRI World Imagery", "ESRI Oceans"))

# print map 
site_map
